A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TRAP by the same authors, with matching core components and overlapping COCO experiments. Text, equations, figures and tables support comparison. v1 ends with references; v2 additionally contains a readable Appendix A.

before.justification: Sections 5–6 report original experiments on 100 COCO image-caption pairs, including attack comparisons and prompt, temperature and threshold analyses.

after.justification: The main text retains original COCO experiments and adds model and defense comparisons. Appendix A reports additional datasets, component ablations, a webpage scenario and computational measurements.

M1.justification: The CLIP/Siamese/diffusion pipeline and three loss components remain. However, the reported masking operation changes from e_com multiplied by mean(A) to elementwise multiplication with A_final, explicitly combining the learned mask and segmentation mask. Revised Algorithm 1 also explicitly decodes and evaluates the final updated candidate. These are localized procedural revisions.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates COCO-based image selection. v2 retains this coverage and adds Flickr8k_sketch, ArtCap artistic images and an e-commerce webpage scenario (Appendix A.2.2 and A.2.6). These introduce different visual domains and page-level input conditions.

E2.justification: v2 adds SSA_CWA and SA_AET to the main attack comparison and the webpage comparison (Tables 1 and 10), alongside retained SPSA, Bandit and unoptimized diffusion. This substantially strengthens comparison against embedding-based attacks; these additions are evaluated methods, not merely citations.

E3.justification: v2 adds Mistral-small-3.2-24B, GPT-4o and CogVLM targets, Robust-LLaVA and additional defense configurations, plus controlled loss-weight, embedding and generator variations. The stated negative-prompt model changes from Llama-3-7B to Llama-3-8B. Table 11 specifies 10,000 steps over 50 iterations for Bandit, whereas v1 states a general 20-by-20 default. TRAP's 100-instance COCO evaluation and 20-by-20 budget remain.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's prompt, temperature, threshold and noise tests, v2 adds CIDER/MirrorCheck defenses, an adversarially trained target, loss-weight and component-removal ablations, embedding/generator substitutions and iterative refinement examples. The original threshold analysis remains represented in Figure 2 despite removal of its separate subsection and redundant plot.

E5.justification: Both versions retain R=100 randomized selections and provide no independent-seed counts or defined confidence intervals. v1 Figures 2–3 contain vertical bar-like marks absent from v2's redrawn Figure 2, but their statistical meaning is never explained. The PDFs do not reliably distinguish removal of uncertainty reporting from a marker-style change.

E6.justification: The original Table 1 cells are retained, while v2 adds substantial results: TRAP obtains 99%, 63% and 94% on Mistral-3.2, GPT-4o and CogVLM. The new webpage experiment reports 51%, 50%, 27% and 17% across its four targets. Additional dataset, defense and ablation outcomes are reported, and Figure 2 curves and runtime values change. The new target/scenario results are not same-setting performance declines.

T1.justification: v2 Section 4.1 replaces the generic selection mapping with an explicit cosine-score/argmax model, formalizes the selection event and adds a perceptual-budget constraint. Section 4.2 distinguishes an unknown user query from the attacker's guidance prompt. These refine formal assumptions and definitions; neither version provides a theorem or proof. Expanded textbook explanations of CLIP and LPIPS do not constitute new theory.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains black-box semantic manipulation of agent preferences. However, the abstract and Discussion replace the blanket 100% success formulation with consistent preference redirection, and replace human-imperceptibility with visually subtle or natural edits. These meaningfully qualify the efficacy and stealth claims while retaining the main contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations connecting proxy prompts to unknown queries, distinctive-feature anchoring to gradient allocation, and perceptual constraints to platform integrity checks. It interprets the new ablations as evidence about semantic-loss importance and component flexibility. Section 8 removes v1's open-source/synthetic-setting qualification, while the appendix acknowledges lower success in webpage settings. These substantially revise mechanism explanations and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: v2 adds a GitHub access pointer, more explicit algorithm bookkeeping, loss coefficients in the ablation tables, alternative model identifiers and a computational breakdown. Most architecture, optimizer and hardware details already appear in v1. Runtime documentation changes, but remains inconsistent: Section 5.2 calls 520/376/110 seconds per-iteration costs, while Table 11 labels them per-sample totals.

R1.justification: The three related-work themes and semantic-versus-pixel positioning remain. v2 condenses the classical attack catalogue, removing references such as GenAttack and NATTACK, and adds literature supporting SSA_CWA, SA_AET, defenses, additional datasets and alternative backbones. These are focused updates to the existing positioning.

P1.justification: Sections 3–4 are extensively rewritten and reorganized, with expanded diffusion, CLIP, LPIPS and optimization explanations. Related work is condensed, Algorithm 1 moves to Appendix A, and threshold discussion is integrated into Section 6.2. The scale of explanatory rewriting and restructuring exceeds routine copyediting.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with clearer Siamese-network and masking stages; Figure 2 expands to six models with a shared legend and revised styling. Table 1 expands, and defense, ablation, dataset and efficiency tables are added. v1's qualitative panel is retained as v2 Figure 3, while its redundant threshold plot is removed and a new iterative-refinement figure appears.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's reliance on weak attack baselines and narrow evaluation through embedding-based comparators, additional model families, defenses, new domains and component ablations (Tables 1–10). These additions make effectiveness and failure conditions more assessable, while softened imperceptibility claims improve calibration. Sparse documentation of the webpage experiment and unresolved numerical/runtime inconsistencies limit reproducibility, but the stronger comparative and diagnostic evidence provides a substantial net improvement.
